# Chapter 8 - sketch answers {.unnumbered}

The questions are in `chapters/08-quantitative-data.qmd`; the sketch answers below are the `\answer{}` texts of the LaTeX script, moved out of the chapter. They are not the only possible answers; the reasoning behind them is what matters.

## Questions from the reading

1. **Good questionnaire question** (@exr-08-good-questionnaire-question) — Five criteria (Peterson, in Ch. 15): **brief, relevant, unambiguous, specific, objective** --- our five failure modes are these, inverted.

2. **Four levels of measurement** (@exr-08-four-levels-of-measurement) — Nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio --- the level decides which operations and which statistics are legal on the data.

3. **Spread** (@exr-08-spread) — Two very different distributions can share a mean --- spread (SD, quartiles) shows whether respondents agree or are split.

4. **P-value** (@exr-08-p-value) — p = the probability of data at least this extreme *if there were no real effect*. It is not the probability the hypothesis is true, and says nothing about the size or importance of the effect.

## Questions for discussion

1. **Your items** (@exr-08-your-items) — Most first drafts contain a double-barrelled item or a leading one. State the level of measurement per item; it decides which descriptive statistics and which test are permitted later.

2. **The analysis plan** (@exr-08-the-analysis-plan) — Naming the one comparison forces the design: two groups or one, paired or independent, which measure. A plan written after the data arrive invites the choice of whichever test happens to be significant.

3. **Effect size** (@exr-08-effect-size) — How large the effect is and whether it matters in practice. Report the effect size and a confidence interval with every test; a small effect in a large sample can be significant and irrelevant at the same time.
